simple.meaning: נֵד (nêd) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a mound , i.e. wave.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 15:8. The surrounding context includes priesthood, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נֵד (H5067) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: נֵד (nêd) / H5067 is traced through Exodus 15:8, Joshua 3:13, Joshua 3:16, Psalms 33:7 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: With the blast of your nostrils, the waters were piled up.

majorEvents.evidenceText: the waters which came down from above stood, and rose up in one heap a great way off, at Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan; and those that went down toward the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, were wholly cut off. Then the people passed over near Jericho.

timeline.evidenceText: With the blast of your nostrils, the waters were piled up.

It shall be that when the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of Yahweh, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan will be cut off. The waters that come down from above shall stand in one heap.”

the waters which came down from above stood, and rose up in one heap a great way off, at Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan; and those that went down toward the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, were wholly cut off. Then the people passed over near Jericho.
He gathers the waters of the sea together as a heap.
He split the sea, and caused them to pass through.
In the day of your planting, you hedge it in. In the morning, you make your seed blossom, but the harvest flees away in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow.
